pr_title: Fix constant initializers if the specified type is different
pr_comments: Notice this PR fixed it by disallowing using such expression on the analyser level, while mine (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/70872) at the compilation stage. But your solution is cleaner and have a test...

Should we allow `const A: int = 1.0`? For function parameters, this is prohibited:

```gdscript
# Error: Type of default value for parameter "x" (float) is not compatible with parameter type (int).
func f(x: int = 1.0):
    pass

# Error: Type of default value for parameter "x" (int) is not compatible with parameter type (float).
func g(x: float = 1):
    pass
```

For variables, this already works correctly and makes sense.

`: float = 1` shouldn't give an error anywhere I guess.

> Should we allow `const A: int = 1.0`? For function parameters, this is prohibited:

I think this should not be allowed. That would then also matches with a lot of other languages.

Solution seems right. 

Maybe `ERR_FAIL`  check for `CallError` is appropriate, at least for future proofing.

> For function parameters, this is prohibited

Function parameters handling is lackluster compared to variables/constants. It does not seem like a deliberate choice but just historical oversight.

For assigning values to changeable assignables (variables/parameters) there is a `use_conversion_assign`. It is present on variable node and on assignment node (lacking again on parameter node), it is used when the type of the incoming thing is either a variant/untyped or a differently typed but convertable.

It was similar logic for constant, but it was neglecting the fact that there will be no future conversion assignment and that reduced value will be used as is.

 > `const A: int = 1.0`, I think this should not be allowed. 
 
I think it makes sense to add at least a warning for cases like this when an initializer is a `LiteralNode`. (Easy to add it to unification PR as such warning applicable to all assignables, not only constants.) 

But for cases such as `var/const x = y` (where y is a convertable but different type), I think there is not much sense in prohibiting it.

Edit: Small note about implementation - `Variant::construct` will be called on every initializer of a constant with an explicit type, no need to do so if types are the same (`const x: int = 0`).

I believe it's okay to allow initializing with a different type if people need it, but there should be a warning because there's a good chance it's a mistake. Especially for the case of constants, since you only assign it once, doesn't make much sense to set a value of a different type.

More testing:

```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorScript

func f1(x: int = 1.0):
    return x

var t2 := 1.0
func f2(x: int = t2):
    return x

var t3 = 1.0
func f3(x: int = t3):
    return x

var t4 = "lalala"
func f4(x: int = t4):
    return x

func _run() -> void:
    print(typeof(f1())) # 2
    print(typeof(f2())) # 2
    print(typeof(f3())) # 3
    print(typeof(f4())) # 4
```

What you showed is lack of `use_conversion_assign` on parameter node.

Edit: Opened a PR to fix that.
I think now the PR is ready for review.

issue_context.title: const PackedArrays iteration issue
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4 beta 13 & 12

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

can't properly iterate over const packed arrays, you can see the output will be a default initialized value and the last element of the array in beta13 and in 12 it will be similar with but with the other elements represented as what seem to be uninitialized memory (random numbers)

### Steps to reproduce

Start a new Project
Add any node and a script to it
add something like this to see it:

```
const array : PackedVector2Array = [Vector2(0,0),Vector2(1,1),Vector2(2,2),Vector2(3,3)]

func _ready() -> void:
	for i in array:
		print(i)
```


### Minimal reproduction project

"N/A" would be faster for you to check in your own projects
comments: I assume that #70873 fixes the issue.

> I assume that #70873 fixes the issue.

Yes, I have tested.

review_comments:
So now the conversion happens for every assignable (variables, constants, parameters) if their initializer is a constant expression. I think it is good. It means that there is no need to set `use_conversion_assign` in such cases because types will always match.

To get that benefit this `if` should merge with previous `if/else` thing, becoming its first `if`. Warning about `NARROWING_CONVERSION` should be decoupled from `if/else` construction and moved above it with condition including hard type check becoming - `specified_type.builtin_type == Variant::INT && initializer_type.is_hard_type() && initializer_type.builtin_type == Variant::FLOAT`.
I did it a little differently: I moved the type incompatibility check above. I think this option is better.
